title: Claude seats stream their output (--output-format stream-json) so stdout silence becomes a real liveness signal and a hung seat is killed for silence again, not only at the 2 h cap
description:
FOLLOW-UP of task-eca3780de7bb44f09ebe669a568bcbda (parent). Filed 2026-09-19 by architect-0f009933 because the human's ruling on the parent asked for it as a separate row (comment-6d395077 on the parent, relayed by governor-f32726f9). dependsOn the parent: this row builds on the parent's corrected silence rule and edits the same agent-spawner.ts.

WHY. After the parent lands, a seat is killed for silence only after a whole window of OBSERVED ticks with no output, no tool child and no tree-CPU growth at all. A hung `claude -p` still burns 125-547 ms of tree CPU per ~60 s (measured on this host through the production probe, parent comment-a96f4b63), so a hung seat lives to MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS (2 h). That is the cost the human accepted, because nothing else tells hung from working today:
- `claude -p` without --output-format writes NOTHING to stdout until it finishes (a working seat measured 50 558 bytes of final stdout and 0 bytes before), so output silence proves nothing;
- a working no-tool-child seat's per-minute CPU (219-1219 ms) overlaps the hung band, so CPU cannot be a kill signal (the ruling).
Streaming the seat's events makes stdout silence mean something again.

WHAT. Spawn Claude seats with `--output-format stream-json` (the Claude argv branch starts at agent-spawner.ts :192, `"-p"`), so every event is a stdout line and `liveness.noteOutput` sees a working seat speak. Then let the silence decision count OUTPUT silence for a seat that streams, so a hung streaming seat is killed at MOE_AGENT_SILENCE_MS instead of the cap. A seat that does not stream keeps the parent's rule.

MEASURE AT PLANNING. These are hazards to measure, not claims (stale-description rail):
1. seat-exit-classifier.ts matches the seat's TEXT on its bounded output tail (SEAT_EXIT_ROSTER, e.g. /You've hit your usage limit(?![.\w])/iu). Its comment at :57-58 warns that a seat printing `rate limit` inside its own JSON output must not park the provider. With every model sentence inside JSON events, prove both (a) the real refusal banners still classify, reason code asserted, and (b) a model-authored refusal sentence inside an assistant event does NOT park the provider.
2. Every reader of the seat's final report (the bounded tail the exit classifier and the ledger fold read; seat-liveness-probe.ts :10-12 names them) must read the `result` event's text, not raw stdout.
3. Measure on the pinned claude build: does stream-json under -p need extra flags (e.g. --verbose)? Does one long assistant message emit anything before it completes (e.g. --include-partial-messages)? A working seat writing one large message must not look silent.
4. packages/runner already parses claude stream-json (packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-stream.ts, schemaVersion claude-stream-json/1). Check reuse under the dependency-edge rail (apps/daemon package.json -> @moe/runner, the pnpm-lock importer, a bare-specifier typecheck probe).
5. Codex seats (`codex exec -`) are out of scope under the v0.1 scope freeze unless the same change is free.

OUT OF SCOPE: the parent's two rules stand. An unobserved tick never counts as silence, and CPU is evidence, never a threshold.
definitionOfDone: Claude seats are spawned with `--output-format stream-json` plus whatever the pinned claude build measurably requires with -p; a spawner arm asserts the exact argv by value.

A working streaming seat is seen speaking: a fake child that emits JSON event lines keeps quietMs below the notice interval, and the seat's final report is read from the `result` event, asserted by value.

The exit classifier still returns its reason code for a real refusal banner in the streamed framing, and a model-authored refusal sentence inside an assistant text event does NOT park the provider. Both are asserted by reason code, not merely by outcome.

A streaming seat that shows no output and no tool child for MOE_AGENT_SILENCE_MS is killed for silence even while its tree CPU grows, and the kill line names it. A non-streaming seat keeps the parent's rule (an arm pins both).
Gate quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json <the touched test files>`, plus `pnpm typecheck`.

GREEN, in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-output-tail.ts only. The file was 105 lines at planning and must stay <= 250.

(1) `export const STREAM_JSON_MAX_LINE_BYTES = 1_048_576;`

(2) `createStreamJsonReport(): { push(chunk: Buffer): Buffer; flush(): Buffer }`. It works on BYTES, splitting at 0x0A; UTF-8 never puts 0x0A inside a multi-byte sequence. Each line has a mode, set by its first byte:
- "{" (0x7B): buffer until the newline, then decode the whole line as UTF-8 and JSON.parse it:
  - an object with type === "result" and a string `result` forwards Buffer.from(result + "\n");
  - a parse failure forwards the raw line plus "\n";
  - any other event forwards nothing.
- Any other first byte: pass through, forwarding the bytes on the push that brought them.
- A buffered line that exceeds STREAM_JSON_MAX_LINE_BYTES switches to skip: drop the buffer and every byte until the next newline.
flush() treats a pending "{" line as ended: `${result}\n` for a result event, otherwise the raw bytes WITHOUT an added newline, because text mode never printed one.
Never prefix-match `{"type":"result"`: the measured key order puts duration_api_ms first.

(3) createSeatOutput({ onBytes, sinks: { stderr, stdout }, streamJson, tail? }), returning a frozen { stdout(chunk), stderr(chunk), close(), seen(), tail() }.
- It creates the OutputTail, and a report only when streamJson is set.
- stdout(chunk): call onBytes(chunk.length), then forward report ? report.push(chunk) : chunk.
- stderr(chunk): call onBytes(chunk.length), then forward the chunk.
- Forwarding: a non-empty buffer sets seen, is written to the matching sink, and is pushed to the tail.
- close(): forwards report.flush() to stdout.
- seen() therefore keeps its text-mode meaning: the seat printed report text or stderr, and protocol events do not count.

comments.content:
MEASURED AT PLANNING (architect-0f009933). Host claude 2.1.277, which is the build seats run: MOE_AGENT_COMMAND defaults to `claude`. Every run used a LOCAL fake API (the source is in the next comment): ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>, a dummy ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1, `--setting-sources "" --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config "say hi"`. No model spend.

1. `claude -p --output-format stream-json` WITHOUT `--verbose` exits 1 and prints on stderr: `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`.

2. With `--verbose --include-partial-messages`, one JSON event per line on stdout, in this order:
- system/init (the first line, ~2 KB);
- system/status {status: "requesting"};
- stream_event: message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta once per text chunk, content_block_stop, message_delta, message_stop;
- assistant (the whole message);
- result.
A dead API (127.0.0.1:9) instead gives system/api_retry per retry, with {attempt, max_retries: 10, retry_delay_ms (38115 by attempt 8), error_status, error}. So a seat waiting on retries IS speaking, and a seat whose request simply hangs is silent.

3. INVARIANT, byte for byte in both runs: text-mode stdout == the `result` event's `result` + "\n".
- OK run: 65 bytes, the model's text.
- 429 run: 114 bytes: `API Error: Request rejected (429) · This request would exceed your account's rate limit. Please try again later.` This is exactly the roster's LIVE sample for claude/rate-limit-429.
stderr in both modes held only the "claude.ai connectors are disabled" warning.

4. The 429 in stream-json:
- an assistant event with message.model "<synthetic>", error "rate_limit" and is_api_error_message true, whose text is the banner;
- then result {subtype: "success", is_error: true, api_error_status: 429, terminal_reason: "api_error", result: <the banner>}.
Exit 1 in both modes.

5. The result event's keys do NOT start with "type"; the first key is "duration_api_ms". Parse the line; never prefix-match it.

6. A model-authored sentence "You've hit your usage limit · resets 3am" in an OK run ends in exit 0, and the classifier's exit-0 rule answers COMPLETED whatever the text. Today that sentence is in the tail too; under this design it is only in the result text, exactly as in text mode.

7. NOT MEASURED: the subscription usage-limit banner ("You've hit your usage limit · resets …"). With an API key, the fake's unified-ratelimit headers still produced the 429 banner. Its place in stream-json is INFERRED from invariant 3, not observed.

8. `--tools` is Edit,Write,Read,Glob,Grep,Bash for coding seats and MCP only for chain seats. There is no Task/Agent tool and no WebFetch, so no in-process subagent or web call can run silently for minutes. A grep for long-poll/waitMs/holdMs/'blocks until' over apps/daemon/src/mcp* found no moe-next MCP handler that long-polls.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 10 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 20 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. DECODE OR PASS RAW JSON. Raw JSON breaks the ^-anchored claude/rate-limit-429 roster pattern. It also floods the wrapper console and logs with one line per token delta. Chosen: decode to exactly what text mode printed. The invariant was measured byte for byte (comment-7c263f1c point 3), so the classifier, the SEAT_EXIT record (lastLine, outputSeen) and the console keep their meaning.
2. WHERE THE DECODER LIVES. A new module would need a .js bridge and a test, which is 11 files. Extending the pure seat-output-tail.ts keeps the row at 10. It also lets agent-spawner.ts (551 lines, over the 400 cap) SHRINK, because its tail/outputSeen/tee block moves into createSeatOutput.
3. CLASSIFY BY STRUCTURED FIELDS (is_error/api_error_status) OR BY TEXT. Kept the text: the roster is text with LIVE provenance, and the invariant keeps that path byte-identical. A structured path is a follow-up only if a banner ever moves.
4. EAGER PASS-THROUGH OF NON-'{' LINES, rather than buffering every line. Eager pass-through keeps plain-text stubs and the existing byte-exact tee arms (a multi-byte char split across chunks) identical.
5. --include-partial-messages IS REQUIRED. Without it, a seat writing one long message (for example a Write of a big file) prints nothing for minutes and would look silent.
